title: regionmatic-kms-escrow-and-operator-least-privilege-shim
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Adds a jurisdiction-aware KMS escrow proxy and RBAC v2 operator-limited role mappings; ships audit enrichment for canonical-region tags and a staged rollout plan.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers running in regulated jurisdictions have asked for finer-grained node/operator controls when a request must be pinned to a geographic key location. This PR introduces 'regionmatic' KMS escrow (a short-lived, provenance-bearing crypto proxy) plus RBAC v2 mappings that enforce least-privilege for operator roles that can request key-wrapping or escrow operations. The goal is to provide: (1) deterministic region pin enforcement early in the routing stack, (2) an operator-limited crypto proxy that performs ephemeral key wrapping only when the requestors' RBAC attributes and audit flags permit it, and (3) canonical-region audit enrichment so downstream auditors can reconstruct residence decisions without leaking sensitive attributes.

What this change does (high level): Implements a small proxy service (kms-escrowd) and an admission/shim layer that validates a request's "region_claim" against customer-configured per-service region policies. Adds RBAC v2 policy templates and a policy compiler hook so operator roles get transient grants (time-limited) instead of broad privileges. Adds audit header canonicalization (X-Redwood-Region-Canonical) and an audit sanitizer that strips ephemeral claims when forwarding to third-party sinks. Adds tests and a canary rollout config to Dedicated and Private installers.

Review conversation (high level):
- Liam Chen: "Left a few nits around error handling and an edge case where the request has both org_region and service_region claims. Can we add a unit test for overlapping claims?"

- Priya Rao: "Concern: audit headers could leak operator identities to external sinks. Are we redacting correctly?"

- Diego Marquez (approval): "Approach looks good for canary; I'd like a follow-up to add telemetry counters for escrow failures and denied grants."
- Diego (merge): "Approved and merged after squash."

Deployment and rollout notes (runbook excerpt):
- Start with canary=2% for Dedicated clusters in us-east-1 with residency policies enabled.
- Monitor metrics: escrow_requests_total, escrow_denied_by_rbac, audit_forward_latency.
- If escrow_denied_by_rbac spikes > 0.2% over baseline, rollback canary and open incident with SRE/Compliance.
- After stable 72h canary, incrementally enable in remaining regions; private installer has a toggle 'regionmatic.enabled'.

Backward compatibility / migration:
- Existing RBAC policies continue to work; the policy compiler emits additional transient grants only when services opt-in by including 'regionmatic: true' in their policy manifest.
- Audit consumers that do not understand X-Redwood-Region-Canonical will continue to receive sealed envelopes; backward-compatible sanitizer leaves legacy headers unchanged when configured.

Security review summary:
- Threat model updated to include escrow replay protection and operator privilege escalation paths.
- Added HMAC-signed audit envelopes and nonce replay cache in kms-escrowd.
- KMS credentials for escrowd are rotated by default and scoped to wrap-only primitives (no decrypt raw key material on disk).

Follow-ups (tracked):
- ENG-2199: add escrow_diagnostics endpoint for SRE debugging behind operator role
- SEC-451: telemetry dashboard to visualize region pin denials and audit forward drops
- ENG-2250: tighter rate limits on operator transient grants and exponential backoff

Merge outcome: squash-merged to main. Commit message included the high-level summary and ticket ENG-2148.
